lines.trans: Three sharp, Suad—my hands have not played four-hand piano since I was twelve!
Your left hand remembers every chord, Rami; just stop counting bars like brick walls!
Sorry! Habit of an architect: one-two-three, four point zero metres to the window!
Think of our courtyard tree swaying gently in Friday wind instead of a ruler.
All right, deep breath... bass chord C, warm G, up to A minor...
Lovely! Hear how rich the lower walnut strings sound beneath my melody on top?
Watch out—here comes that fast turn at bar sixteen where I always rush!
Listen to my right hand breathe first, then step in like an old friend answering.
One, two, step in... hey, middle D sang right between our hands without a hitch!
Bravo, Rami! Your old cartography professor is going to beam from ear to ear!
Wait—look out the arched window: Salma and Ziad are carrying four hot tins outside!
One more run from the top, partner, while the summer berry cakes cool in the shade!

See you soon!

meanings.note: Agrees with the speaker's gender: a man says أنا آسف, a woman says أنا آسفة.

examples.trans: I am very sorry for the delay.
Sorry for the bother, sir.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for both casual 'yes / yeah' and 'oh! / ah!' upon noticing something.

examples.trans: Oh, the door opened! Thank you.
Yes, eight rooms and eight keys.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective placed after a definite noun (السلم الأخير 'the final scale'). Feminine: أخيرة, plural: أخيرين.

examples.trans: This is the final scene in today's episode.
We played the final scale in complete calm.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Used as a question word or indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Which tub of butter did you bring?

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

meanings.note: Form IV verbal noun from عاد, used for rehearsals, replays, and another try.

examples.text: هاي آخر إعادة للمشهد قبل العرض.
examples.trans: This is the last run-through of the scene before the show.

examples.text: بعد إعادة سريعة صارت الجملة واضحة.
examples.trans: After one quick repeat, the line became clear.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببتسم, بيبتسم).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
He smiled when he saw his brother.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بستعجل, بيستعجل).

examples.trans: Hurry, the guests are coming down the stairs!
Do not rush to go upstairs.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'twelve'; before a singular counted noun it takes -r: اطنعشر دقة ('twelve chimes').

examples.trans: The clock tower chimed twelve!
Here is twelve dinars change.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنتبه, بينتبه).

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من الخشب الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low beam.
Be careful of the corner chair.

meanings.note: Exactly, precisely.

examples.text: هذا اللي كنت بدي أحكيه بالضبط.
examples.trans: This is exactly what I wanted to say.
We arrived at nine o'clock sharp.

meanings.note: Used directly before nouns or pronouns (بدل ستة 'instead of six') and before ما + verb (بدل ما تستنى 'instead of waiting').

examples.text: اشرب شاي سخن بالنعنع بدل القهوة بالليل.
examples.trans: Drink hot mint tea instead of coffee at night.

examples.text: ضل معنا تلات أيام بس بدل أسبوع كامل.
examples.trans: We only have three days left instead of a whole week.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'without', used identically to MSA.

examples.text: شاي أحمر بدون سكر لو سمحتي.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please.
I entered the booking without my glasses!

meanings.note: Refers to being outdoors or outside a specific location.

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Commonly heard in Amman to applaud music, baking, or a clever idea. Followed by عليك/عليكي for 'well done to you!'.

examples.trans: Bravo! The piano playing was wonderful!

examples.text: برافو عليكي يا نور، الخطة ممتازة.
examples.trans: Well done, Nour, the plan is excellent.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببرد, بيبرد).

examples.trans: The cake is cooling on the rack right now.
The radiator is starting to get cold at the bottom.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'then, next, afterwards' (وبعدين 'and then').

examples.trans: Lift the handle first, and then push.
Have some tea and then we will talk.

meanings.note: The musical instrument.

examples.trans: The sound of the piano is warm and calm.
I learned piano when I was young.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'bass', referring to the bass line, bass guitar, or upright bass.

examples.text: خط البيز هو اللي بيمسك إيقاع الأغنية.
examples.trans: The bass line is what holds the rhythm of the song.

examples.text: صوت البيز كان واطي شوي بالبروفة.
examples.trans: The bass sound was a bit low in the rehearsal.

meanings.note: Preposition 'between, among'.

examples.trans: Today you are mending things between two brothers!
The table is between the window and the door.

meanings.note: Used to contrast two different situations or actions happening at the same time.

examples.text: بنرتب القاعة بينما بتبرد الكيكة بالظل.
examples.trans: We tidy the hall while the cake cools in the shade.

examples.text: طلعنا الساحة بينما الحجرة التالتة بتستنى.
examples.trans: We carried it out while the third stone is waiting.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian and Levantine word used as a possessive marker, similar to "of" or "'s".

examples.text: اليوم آخر يوم بأسبوع التجربة تبعك.
examples.trans: Today is the last day of your trial week.
My brother's piano teacher!

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from حوّل ('to divert/turn'): a side turn in a road or trail, or a call extension.

examples.text: خد التحويلة اللي على إيدك اليمين.
examples.trans: Take the turnoff on your right-hand side.

examples.text: في تحويلة جديدة على طريق المطار.
examples.trans: There is a new detour on the airport road.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.en: to sway back and forth gently
meanings.note: Form VI verb from مال ('to lean / tilt'), expressing gentle rhythmic swaying.

examples.trans: The branches sway with the breeze.
The lanterns are swaying calmly.

meanings.note: Form V verb from نفس ('breath').

examples.text: فتحت الشباك عشان أتنفس هوا نضيف.
examples.trans: I opened the window to breathe fresh air.

examples.text: بعد ما رتبنا القائمة، قدرت أتنفس براحة.
examples.trans: Once we organized the list, I could breathe easily.

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for berries/mulberries (singulative توتة 'one berry').

examples.trans: The berry and almond cake turned out delicious!
We have an old mulberry tree in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Active participle of إجا ('to come'): means 'on the way / arriving' (جايين 'they are coming') and after a time noun 'next' (الأسبوع الجاي 'next week').

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs now.
We will see you next week!

meanings.note: Day of the week Friday, literally 'gathering day'.

examples.trans: Every Friday morning we drink coffee.
Friday is a lovely day in Amman.

جنّن.gloss: to amaze; drive wild; look or taste wonderful

meanings.en: to amaze; drive wild; look or taste wonderful
meanings.note: Form II geminate verb. In Levantine speech, بيجنن ('it drives one crazy') is one of the warmest compliments for food, music, or places.

examples.trans: The smell of pastries from the morning is amazing!

examples.text: العزف اليوم جنن كل اللي قاعدين.
examples.trans: Today's playing amazed everyone sitting there.

meanings.note: Everyday masculine noun for an answer or musical response (plural: أجوبة).

examples.trans: A breath first and a second answer on the key.
We are waiting for an answer from City Hall tomorrow.

meanings.note: Collective noun for walnuts; خشب جوز is walnut wood. (Not to be confused with جوز 'husband; pair', a different everyday sense.)

examples.trans: I bought a kilo of walnuts at the market.
The cake has walnuts and honey in it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحمل, بيحمل).

examples.text: بتحمل مفك بكل مكان يا طارق!
examples.trans: You carry a screwdriver everywhere, Tariq!
He picked up the wrong blue bag at the station.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حيطان.

examples.trans: We hung the mirror on the wall.
Stone walls keep the coolness in summer.

meanings.note: Standard word for a geographical or digital map.

examples.trans: Look at the folded map inside the box.
We drew a small map of the street.

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine feminine noun (from Classical أذن). Dual دينين is used as the normal plural for ears.

examples.text: سمعت الخبر من دان لدان بسرعة.
examples.trans: I heard the news from ear to ear quickly.

examples.text: حطيت إيدي على داني عشان أسمع أوضح.
examples.trans: I cupped my hand to my ear to hear more clearly.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of دائما ('always').

examples.trans: I always walk fast on the first day.
Noon traffic is always slow.

دخل.gloss: to enter; come in; go in

meanings.en: to enter; come in; go in
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بدخل, بيدخل).

examples.text: تفضل ادخل من المطر يا أستاذ.
examples.trans: Please come in out of the rain, sir.

examples.text: الزوجين دخلوا غرفة ستة قبل ساعة.
examples.trans: The couple checked into room six an hour ago.

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برد, بيرد).

examples.text: اشربي شاي أول وبعدين ردي عالجرس.
examples.trans: Drink tea first and then answer the bell.
Nobody answered the phone at the station.

meanings.note: Extremely common Levantine preposition meaning 'like' or 'similar to'.

examples.trans: I want a glass of tea like yesterday.
Do it the way I taught you.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: Active participle of سمع ('to hear'), standard in Jordanian for 'can you hear?' (سامعني؟).

examples.trans: I hear you clearly on the phone.
Do you hear the sound of a car outside the gate?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سخنة, plural: سخنين).

examples.trans: Drink a glass of hot tea first.
Pour the hot water into the pot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سريعة, plural: سريعين).

examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast!
Quick service and a kind smile.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 16; before a counted singular noun it may appear as سطاش or سطاعشر.

examples.text: مدام سعاد رح تكتب السطاش مازورة الناقصة.
examples.trans: Madam Suad is going to write the sixteen missing bars.

examples.text: صفينا سطاش فنجان أبيض على الرف.
examples.trans: We lined up sixteen white cups on the shelf.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شبابيك.

examples.trans: The window overlooks the courtyard tree.
We painted the wooden shutters in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a tree.

examples.text: قطفنا ليمون أصفر طازة من شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: We picked fresh yellow lemons from the courtyard tree.

examples.text: ظل الشجرة بيبرد القعدة وقت الظهر.
examples.trans: The shade of the tree cools the seating area at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: شريكة). Plural: شركاء.

examples.trans: Great work today, partner!

examples.text: همه شركاء بالمخبز من عشر سنين.
examples.trans: They have been partners in the bakery for ten years.

meanings.note: In everyday Jordanian directions, شمال (shmaal) means 'left' (contrast شَمال shamaal 'north').

examples.trans: Turn left at the street corner.
The key is on the shelf to your left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صحاب.

examples.trans: Who is the owner of the blue suitcase?
We became friends from the first day.

meanings.note: Describes a pure musical note, clear sky (سما صافية), or clear broth.

examples.text: نغمة البيانو طلعت صافية متل المي.
examples.trans: The piano note rang out crystal clear.

examples.text: انشالله تضل السما صافية طول نهار التنين.
examples.trans: Hopefully the sky stays clear all day Monday.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: The season of summer.

examples.trans: Evenings in Amman are pleasant in summer.
Our rent is paid until next summer.

meanings.note: Broken plural صواني ('serving trays' or 'oven baking pans').

examples.text: جهزنا تلات صواني خبز عشان تدخل الفرن الفجر.
examples.trans: We prepped three trays of bread to go into the oven at dawn.

examples.text: نور حملت صينية الشاي بالنعنع للساحة.
examples.trans: Nour carried the mint tea tray out to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طالعة, plural: طالعين).

examples.trans: Count on me, I am heading right out!
We are going up to the third floor.

meanings.note: Collective noun for bricks or building blocks; حيط طوب is a brick wall.

examples.trans: The house is built of brick and stone.
They brought new bricks for the wall.

meanings.note: Describes kind-hearted people (ناس طيبين) and pleasant smells/tastes (ريحة طيبة); standalone طيب means 'alright / well then'.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
The coffee smells wonderful in the morning!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: عادات.

examples.trans: Usually we open the gate at seven.
Drinking morning coffee is a nice habit.

meanings.note: Plural command form from عدّ ('to count') with the 'them' ending.

examples.text: حافظ على العدّ عشان ما تسبق الإيقاع.
examples.trans: Keep the count so you don't rush ahead of the rhythm.

examples.text: خلصنا عدّ الكراسي قبل ما يوصلوا الضيوف.
examples.trans: We finished counting the chairs before the guests arrived.

meanings.note: Arabic expresses age with عمر + possessive suffix: عمره تمانين سنة ('its/his age is eighty years').

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
He has lived in this quarter all his life.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عميقة, plural: عميقين).

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
The old well is very deep.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعزف, بيعزف).

examples.trans: I am still waiting for you to play the scale!

examples.text: الكبير كان يعزف بيانو كل جمعة.
examples.trans: The older boy used to play piano every Friday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غلطات.

examples.trans: This is not your fault at all.
We fixed the slip-up in two minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for singing; a song is أغنية.

examples.trans: My grandmother sings while she cooks.
We all sang at his birthday.

meanings.note: Active participle of فكر used as a stative predicate meaning 'remembers' (أنا فاكر 'I remember').

examples.trans: Do you remember where we put the keys?

examples.text: كلنا فاكرين القصة اللي حكيتها زمان.
examples.trans: We all remember the story you told back then.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفكر, بيفكر).

examples.trans: I thought it was lost when we sold the house!
We thought the matter through calmly.

meanings.note: Used as a preposition or adverb meaning 'above', 'over', or 'upstairs'.

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Colloquial Levantine noun for cooling shade under a tree or awning (distinct from the particle/preposition في).

examples.trans: Sit in the shade under the mulberry tree.
The shade in the garden refreshes the spirit in summer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for soon or near.

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: The main interrogative word for asking about manner or state.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?
Tell me how to find the shop.

meanings.note: Refers to a single, whole cake, or a distinct slice (singulative form of kēk).

examples.text: كيكة الليمون الصفرا طلعت من الفرن.
examples.trans: The yellow lemon cake came out of the oven.
We sliced the cake into six equal pieces.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ألحان.

examples.trans: She played old melodies on the piano.
This gentle tune is familiar to me.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Standard Arabic conservatory/musicians' term (from Italian misura) for one bar of music.

examples.text: عزفت سعاد أول أربع مازورات من الفالس.
examples.trans: Suad played the first four bars of the waltz.

examples.text: اللحن بيوقف بنص المازورة الرابعة والعشرين.
examples.trans: The melody stops in the middle of the twenty-fourth bar.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أمتار.

examples.trans: The table is ten metres away.
The courtyard is eight metres wide.

meanings.note: Polite everyday Jordanian address for an adult woman or female guest.

examples.trans: Good morning, madam, please come in!
The room is booked under Madam Suad.

meanings.note: Used for measuring and drawing crisp straight lines on signs or labels.

examples.text: سطرت نور الملصقين بالمسطرة وقلم الحبر الأسود.
examples.trans: Nour ruled both labels with a straightedge and a black ink pen.

examples.text: قيس الحروف بالمسطرة عشان تطلع بوسط اللوحة.
examples.trans: Measure the letters with the ruler so they sit centered on the sign.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: معمارية, plural: معماريين).

examples.trans: I am an architectural acoustics engineer.

examples.text: حجر عمان إله طابع معماري جميل.
examples.trans: Amman stone has a beautiful architectural character.

meanings.note: From قوس, an arch or bow: arched windows are شبابيك مقوسة.

examples.trans: The mosque's door is arched and tall.
They have old arched windows.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; مهندس معماري means 'architect'. Plural: مهندسين.

examples.trans: His brother is a skilled architect in Amman.
The engineer inspected the walls of the old building.

meanings.note: Often used to mean 'the same' when followed by a noun, or as a reflexive.

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
We took the exact same bus in the morning.

نوتة.gloss: sheet music; musical score; pocket notepad

meanings.en: sheet music; musical score; pocket notepad
meanings.note: Used across the Levant for printed or handwritten musical notation (نوتة موسيقية).

examples.text: فتحت سعاد نوتة البيانو القديمة عالصفحة الأولى.
examples.trans: Suad opened the old piano score to page one.

examples.text: كتب المؤلف النوتة بحبر أسود واضح.
examples.trans: The composer wrote the score in clear black ink.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine feminine noun from هدي ('to calm down'). بهداوة means 'gently / calmly / take it easy'.

examples.text: امشي بهداوة يا سيدي، معنا وقت.
examples.trans: Walk gently, sir—we have time.
With calmness, every knot untangles.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A little air got into the old pipes.
Morning air in Amman is crisp and clean.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Stretched wire or gut string on a piano, oud, or violin.

examples.text: المطرقة بتضرب الأوتار التلاتة فبيطلع صوت صافي.
examples.trans: The hammer strikes the three strings and produces a clear note.

examples.text: كل وتر بالبيانو مشدود بدقة عالية.
examples.trans: Every string inside the piano is tensioned with great precision.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian adjective from وسط ('middle'); pairs naturally with المفتاح الوسطاني and ري الوسطى.

examples.text: المفتاح الوسطاني بالبيانو كان عالق من الرطوبة.
examples.trans: The middle key on the piano was stuck from dampness.

examples.text: الطاولة الوسطانية بالساحة بتاخد أحلى شمس.
examples.trans: The middle table in the courtyard catches the nicest sunshine.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.text: وقفوا كل شي، قديش الساعة هلا؟
examples.trans: Stop everything — what time is it right now?
The driver pulled the car up by the kerb.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The green pharmacy is on your right.
We hung the board to the right of the desk.

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
